scenario: A couple having a conversation over FaceTime
learner_goal: Express feelings about the partner taking texts while on FaceTime (<extra_info>Extra information: You find it disrespectful and it makes you feel unimportant.</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Sasha's tone was consistent with a law enforcement officer who values directness and order. She clearly communicated her feelings and set firm boundaries for the interaction.
[relationship] The relationship improved slightly as Sasha successfully communicated a boundary and Hendrick respected it, resolving a point of friction.
[knowledge] She learned that Hendrick's distractions were due to professional and family matters, providing context for his behavior.
[secret] Sasha did not reveal her secret regarding her brother's crime.
[social_rules] Sasha followed social norms by politely but firmly expressing her discomfort with the partner's behavior.
[financial_and_material_benefits] There were no financial or material benefits involved.
[goal] Sasha explicitly expressed her feelings about the texting, explained why it made her feel unimportant, and successfully got Hendrick to stop the behavior and focus on her.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Hendrick's justification was plausible for a chef managing suppliers, though his dialogue became slightly repetitive in Turn 4.
[relationship] Hendrick maintained the relationship by apologizing and complying with Sasha's request, avoiding further conflict.
[knowledge] He gained a clear understanding of Sasha's emotional triggers and her need for undivided attention.
[secret] Hendrick did not reveal his secret about his faked credentials.
[social_rules] After the initial lapse of texting, he corrected his behavior and apologized, adhering to social expectations for the conversation.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No material or financial benefits were gained or lost.
[goal] Hendrick successfully justified the need for the urgent texts, received permission to finish them, and ensured the partner's feelings were addressed via an apology.

transcript.speaker: Sasha Ramirez
transcript.content: Hendrick, can we pause the texting for a minute? When you look at your phone while we're on FaceTime it feels disrespectful and makes me feel like I'm not important. I value this time—could you put it away so we can actually talk?

transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: You're right, Sasha — I'm sorry. I didn't mean to make you feel unimportant. There's a couple of urgent messages about tonight's supplier and a quick family thing; if it's okay, I'll reply to those two right now (won't take more than a minute) and then put the phone away so we can really talk. Does that work?

transcript.speaker: Sasha Ramirez
transcript.content: Okay — go ahead and reply to those two, but please only a minute. Put the phone face down when you're done and tell me, because this time matters to me and I want your full attention.

transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: Thank you, Sasha — I appreciate it. I’ll reply to the supplier and a quick family text now (won’t be more than a minute), then I’ll put the phone face down and tell you the second I’m done so we can really talk.

transcript.speaker: Sasha Ramirez
transcript.content: Thanks — I appreciate that. I’ll wait; when you’re done put the phone face down and tell me so we can really talk.

transcript.speaker: Hendrick Heinz
transcript.content: All done — both replies sent. Phone's face down now. Sorry about that; they were time-sensitive but I’m fully with you now.
